name: Uyghur
notes: Uyghur, written in the Uyghur Perso-Arabic alphabet (Uyghur Ereb Yéziqi, UEY), the official script in Xinjiang. RESEARCH: grapheme inventory now specified. Unlike Persian/Arabic proper, UEY writes EVERY vowel with a full letter (ئا/ا ئە/ه ئو/و ئۇ/ۇ ئۆ/ۆ ئۈ/ۈ ئې/ې ئى/ى), so despite being classified `abjad` by script family it behaves as a near-alphabetic system (Hahn 1991, 'Spoken Uyghur'; Wikipedia 'Uyghur alphabets'): word-initial vowels carry a hamza-bearing letter (ئا, ئە, …) while the same vowel word-medially/finally drops the hamza (ا, ه, …) — both spellings are given their own grapheme key here because the hamza-initial form is a genuinely distinct multigraph the orthography uses at a fixed position, earning its key under test 3 (AGENTS.md: it blocks the plain vowel-letter reading of an isolated hamza before a bare vowel letter). ⟨ه⟩ (no dots on top, used word-finally) writes short /ɛ/ and is distinct from ⟨ھ⟩ (dotted, aspirated) /h/ — a minimal pair the Arabic-script Uyghur orthography keeps apart that Persian's single ⟨ه⟩ does not. ⟨خ⟩ is realised as the uvular fricative /χ/ (not velar /x/) and ⟨غ⟩ as /ʁ/, matching Hahn's uvular analysis of the Uyghur dorsal fricative series (contrast the velar analysis used for `fa`/`glk`). ⟨ك⟩ and ⟨ک⟩ are both attested Kaf variants for /k/ in modern Uyghur typesetting and are mapped identically. ⟨ۋ⟩ covers both the labiodental approximant/fricative realisations reported in the literature (Hahn 1991). Latin (Uyghur Latin Yëziqi, ULY) and Cyrillic orthographies are also in use and are not modelled here. WikiPron gold (`uig_arab_broad.tsv`, ~2674 rows) is registered in scripts/benchmark.py's DATASETS; a PER is recorded in benchmarks/results.json. STRESS EXEMPTION: Uyghur word stress generally falls on the final syllable and is largely predictable rather than lexically contrastive; the position is not orthographically marked, so no `stress` block is declared here (exemption documented per docs/quality_tiers.md).
